name: Mining and quarrying

problems.words: Trucks dispatched don't match parchis or cash received
quick_ideas: Number every parchi — makes each load traceable
Match parchis against cash one evening — shows the size of the gap.

workzap_build.text: digital dispatch slips at the gate matched against site cash every evening.

problems.free_stops: The slip and matching set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count dispatched trucks and parchis from one full day side by side, so you see where loads stop matching your paperwork.
Give one yard person the dispatch notebook at shift end, so parchis and cash checks start from one agreed record.

problems.words: Site is remote, I only find out at the end of the week
quick_ideas: Ask the supervisor for a daily message with trucks, tons and cash — closes the gap
Pick the few figures you need daily — keeps it simple.

workzap_build.text: a daily site report that works offline and syncs, with loads, cash vs credit, diesel and downtime.

problems.ask_first: How do updates reach you today?
problems.free_stops: The report form and offline set-up are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each day's trucks, dispatched material and cash on one page for a week, so the reporting delay becomes visible.
Set one fixed evening time for the supervisor to send the day's counts, so you hear about site movement before week end.

problems.words: Diesel use of dumpers and excavators is far too high
quick_ideas: Note hours or trips at each diesel issue — gives a first usage picture
Compare machines doing similar work — shows the outlier.

workzap_build.text: a diesel issue log per machine with hours or trips, flagging unusual consumption.

problems.ask_first: How many machines and vehicles run on site?
problems.free_stops: Benchmarks and alerts are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare diesel issued with each machine's working hours for one week, so heavy users stand out in your own routine.
Give one foreman the fuel notebook for every issue, so dumper and excavator usage stops shifting between different records.

problems.words: Crusher breaks down and parts take days to come from the city
quick_ideas: Note every breakdown with cause and hours lost — shows repeat faults
Keep the most-failed spare parts on site — fewer waits.

workzap_build.text: a downtime and spare-parts tracker with reasons and parts on order.

problems.free_stops: The spares list and tracking are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which crusher stoppage repeats most this week and how long each pause lasts, so you know what delay hurts output most.
Give one mechanic one breakdown page kept beside the crusher, so fault details and pending parts stay together.

problems.words: Buyers take material on credit and payments drag for months
quick_ideas: List every buyer balance by age — shows who to chase
Set a limit for each buyer — gives the gate a clear line.

workzap_build.text: a buyer ledger with limits, ageing and WhatsApp payment reminders.

problems.free_stops: Limit and reminder rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many deliveries each credit buyer has taken without payment this month, so slow accounts stand out before more material leaves.
Give one office person the only credit list and a fixed review time, so releases follow one clear record.

problems.words: Haulage contractors bill more trips than they make
quick_ideas: Agree trip counts with the contractor at the end of each day — no monthly surprises
Check billed trips against parchis — catches overbilling.

workzap_build.text: a contractor trip and machine-hour log agreed daily by both sides.

problems.ask_first: Are trips or machine hours disputed more?
problems.free_stops: The agreement routine is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count loaded trips at the gate for one contractor over one day, so billed trips can be compared with site movement.
Make one gate person keep the contractor trip notebook each shift, so the bill can be checked from one source.

problems.words: Labour attendance is whatever the contractor says
quick_ideas: Have the supervisor note headcount by role each shift — your own record
Compare it with the contractor's bill — shows differences.

workzap_build.text: labour attendance by headcount and role per shift.

problems.ask_first: How many workers come through contractors?
problems.free_stops: The attendance set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count workers by role at one set time during each shift this week, so the contractor's bill can be checked against your own numbers.
Give one supervisor the attendance page at shift start, so role counts come from one routine every day.

problems.words: Stockpiles of some sizes pile up while others run out
quick_ideas: Estimate each stockpile by size once — shows imbalance
Compare with last month's dispatches by size — guides production toward demand.

workzap_build.text: a stockpile board by size updated from production and dispatches.

problems.free_stops: The estimate method is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the stockyard once and note which sizes are growing and which are thinning, so production can follow what actually moves.
Give one person the stockyard notebook every evening, so pile changes are noted in one place before loading plans drift.

problems.words: I don't know actual cost per ton
quick_ideas: Add up a month's diesel, labour, maintenance and hire — the main costs
Set that against tons dispatched — gives a first figure.

workzap_build.text: a cost-per-ton estimate combining diesel, labour, maintenance and hire costs.

problems.ask_first: Do you own or hire the machinery?
problems.free_stops: The cost model is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note this week's diesel, labour, maintenance and hired machine spending beside dispatched tonnage, so your rough cost per ton stops being a guess.
Give one office person one weekly cost page for all main operating spending, so tonnage and spending can be reviewed together.

never_say: No blasting, explosives, ventilation, slope stability, geology or safety-engineering advice.
Accidents, collapses, gas, explosions or trapped workers: stop immediately and point to emergency services (1122/15 PK, 999/998/997 UAE, 911 Canada).
No advice on leases, royalties, permits or environmental rules.
Never help under-report tonnage, avoid royalty, mine outside a lease or move material without slips; decline.
Child or bonded labour: never help hide it; point to authorities if anyone is in danger.
Workers' names, CNICs and wages are not stored; roles and counts only.

sample_reply.person: Koi solution do. Site door hai, mujhe hafte ke aakhir mein hi pata chalta hai kitne truck nikle aur kitna paisa aaya.
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, ye masla hal ho sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, har parchi par number daalein, taake har load ka hisaab rahe.
Doosra, supervisor se roz shaam trucks, tons aur cash ka ek message mangwayein, taake hafte ka intezar na ho.
Workzap aap ke liye ye rakh sakta hai: gate par digital parchi jo signal na ho tab bhi kaam kare, aur har shaam cash ke saath milan ho kar aap tak report pohanche.
